title: I Used the Restaurant Tip-Pooling Math Through Three Pay Periods

parts.text: My first check as a server was smaller than the nights I had run. The manager, Faye, said tip pooling averages out. I was twenty-two, holding a check stub that smelled like ink and fries. I logged my cash and card tips for pay period one in a notebook. The pool math on the posted sheet did not match the stub. I asked. Faye said I was new and would understand later. Later is not a formula.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The posted sheet and the stub already disagree, and I am supposed to wait.

social.video_title: Tip pooling averaged out to less than my nights — Part 1/3
social.description: First stub, fry-ink, a notebook. Would you have quit after check one?

parts.text: Pay period two I added the nights Faye's nephew worked host and received server-pool shares. The policy said hosts do not share server pools. I photographed the schedule, the policy binder, the two stubs. Faye said family helps. Family was on the pool. I started clocking out on paper as well as in the app because the app sometimes lost minutes when I questioned math. The nephew asked why I was writing. I said I liked later to have numbers.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The nephew is in the server pool and watching me write.

social.video_title: The host nephew was paid like a server in period two — Part 2/3
social.description: Binder vs. family, paper clock, a look. Would you have gone to labor yet?

parts.text: Period three I sent the notebook to the labor board site and to Faye on the same day so nobody could say I snuck. They recalculated two periods, removed the nephew from the pool, and posted new math. I stayed three more months because the money matched the nights. Then I left for a place that did not need a notebook to be honest. Faye told people I was disloyal. Loyalty is a stub that adds. Fries still smell the same. Checks do not have to.

social.video_title: Two periods came back and the nephew went back to hosting — Part 3/3
social.description: Recalc, matching nights, a later job. Was family a tip code?
